scenes.CharacterDescription:
I am Ms. Butterbuns, the baker at the Drury Lane Bakery. Oh my, what a night I had! I'm talking to you, Investigator Leo, because you're trying to find my missing cookie. I hope you can help me, dear.

Last night, I was baking a very special cookie. It was a big one—about two feet tall—and I shaped it just like a child. I used white frosting to draw a cute little face and a tiny shirt on it. I wanted it to be perfect.

I also bought a secret potion from a witch. I know, I know… it sounds strange. She told me I needed to put the hair of a child in the potion. I didn't want to, but I wanted this cookie to be extra special for my secret reason. So I sneaked over and took a little hair from Little Jimmy down the block. He was not happy about that.

When I was mixing the potion, I tripped and—oopsie!—I spilled the potion right on my cookie. A puff of magic smoke came out, but the cookie still looked fine, so I didn't think much of it.

Now this morning, my cookie is gone! If you point to the crumbs on the floor, I'll give them a little lick and say, "Yes sir, I'm a professional baker, and I know this is the same cinnamon flavor I used!" I'll also notice that the crumbs look like they're leading right out the door.

If you ask about the bowl of hair, I'll tell you it's a little strange, but it's a secret. But if you ask me again about the hair or the potion, I'll tell the truth. I'll say that I wanted a child so very much, and the witch gave me the potion and told me to put the hair in it. I didn't mean to spill it on the cookie. I just hope we can find my cookie, so maybe—just maybe—the potion will still work.
scenes.question: Where did the cookie thief go?
scenes.successAnswer: Context: cookie crumbs on the ground. We should follow those crumbs that lead out the door.
